Girdwood Public Safety Advisory Committee Regular Meeting
                           August 11, 2026
                              Minutes Final

This meeting will be held via Teams with in-person attendance at the Girdwood Community Room, 250 Egloff Dr.

The Girdwood Public Safety Advisory Committee operates under the Girdwood Public Meetings Standards of Conduct.

7PM Call to order, Luke Niedringhaus, co-chair
Roll call: Attending are Luke Niedringhaus, Debra Croghan and Amanda Tuttle.
Quorum confirmed.
GBOS: Amanda Tuttle

Agenda approval for August 11 2026 meeting  LN/AT         Assent
Minutes approval from June 9 2026 meeting   LN/AT         Assent

Announcements/Introductions/Presentation:
See meeting packet for information on Smart911 and sprinkler distribution.

Old Business:

        1. QR code for PSAC and New FAQ info.
QR code is posted on library, community room and post office bulletin boards.
Info sheet for Police Service in Girdwood was revised to separate PSAC info from Police information.
Staff is seeking approval from WPD before posting.

        2.  Progress with Traffic and Traffic control study of Hightower Road.
Follow up from earlier request from the Municipal Manager is that Phase 1 of Holtan Hills was shared with GBOS:

With respect to Holtan Hills, the plat application for phase 1 of the project has been submitted and the Traffic
Department has determined that the trip generation for phase 1 does not hit the minimum threshold for imposing the
traffic study requirement. That said, this may change as platting actions for additional phases of the project come
forward.

PSAC still wants a traffic study for the area, including Alyeska Highway. Alyeska Highway is DOT right-of-way.

Motion:
GHEC moves to have Amanda Tuttle write a letter for GBOS to review at their regular meeting on MON Aug 17.
Motion by LN/2nd DC
Assent

Resolution 2025-14 is the prior GBOS resolution on this topic.
Amanda plans to draft the letter and have it circulated to PSAC members, provide final to GBOS for their meeting
Monday.

        3.  Update on GBOS Public Safety Liaison meeting with DOT:
Amanda Tuttle has not been successful in meeting with DOT Southcentral Region director. Position is currently filled
by Katherine Keith, in an “acting” capacity. Katherine Keith is Deputy Commissioner for the AKDOTPF.
Topics that she was going to take up with them are:
    •   Alyeska Highway proposed speed limit changes and countermeasures to support new speed zones
    •   Alyeska Highway bike path concerns
In addition, recent death of a bore tide surfer has highlighted Turnagain Arm concerns

For reference, meeting packet from June 2026 includes the study and recommendation from prior director Sean
Holland.

Group discusses trying to establish consistent communication with DOT on a local level.
Debra Croghan will reach out to local DOT to see about getting participation at PSAC.


               Girdwood Public Safety Advisory Committee is a sub-committee to the Girdwood Board of Supervisors

4.  Public Safety Contract after 2027:
Ideas to be considered in next contract cycle (starting Jan 1 2028)
    •   Potential for enforcement of Municipal code
    •   Longer contract period
PSAC requests that the police activities report include general location of the activity reported: Town Center Area, Old
Girdwood, Resort Area.

        5. MOA tax levy funds for Police IT
Projects must be for Girdwood use. Proposed List needed for GBOS AUG meeting
PSAC makes no recommendation. GVSA manager and WPD will know better what equipment is needed and fills the
funding requirements.

        6. MOA tax levy funds for Tourism Improvement Projects
Projects must be for promotion of tourism.
Ideas discussed:
    •   signage needs to direct visitors to trails and resources
    •   public restrooms in high density visitation areas, such as the Girdwood Station Mall
    •   trash service in high density visitation areas, such as Girdwood Station Mall
    •   additional signage to encourage visitors to use facilities such as the US Forest Service, which has restrooms
      and visitor information
    •   Potential for creating a rest-stop with restrooms along the highway north or south of Girdwood.

Motion:
PSAC moves to recommend that GBOS focus on TIPS projects to focus on trash and bathrooms, starting at the entry
to the valley near the Girdwood Station Mall.
Motion by DC/2nd LN
Motion carries by assent

        7. GVSA Public Safety Budget
Proposed budget is reviewed. Police services are contractually set. Funding for other projects such as towing, etc are
not specifically called out. Funding request for Wind River Bear Institute was received, some amount of MISC funds
could be used for that.

New Business:
        8.  Discuss any new and ongoing Girdwood public safety concerns (see meeting packet)
Mini e-dirt bikes on parks, trails and roads: no discussion on this, response this summer by staff was social media
post regarding what types of equipment are allowed on trails, roads, etc.

Items discussed:
    •   Complaint of refrigerator truck at merc impeding roadway and causing noise requests PSAC action on this for
      2027 Forest Fair. Discussed but no action taken.
    •   Request to eliminate passing lane on Alyeska Highway - this is added to Debra’s list to discuss with DOT
    •   Request to create formal crosswalk at Ruane Rd for access to Lower INHT. – added to Debra’s list
    •   Brewery overflow parking was brought up at last meeting. Debra wants to revisit this and suggests making
       the no parking signs two-sided so that they are more visible to drivers. Road signage is MOA traffic dept
        responsibility – Debra Crogan to reach out to MOA traffic dept.
    •   Turnagain Arm Access – Andy Morrison has been working with DOT and Sen. Murkowski’s office regarding
       improving emergency access to Turnagain Arm and replacing access that was removed with highway work
        several years ago. Ideas include access just south of Girdwood, which would require gravel to create boat
       launch and an area north of Girdwood between pullout 2 and 3, where there is a cliff that rescue boat could be
          lifted down to water. This would require GFD to have a ladder truck capable of operating in this way.
    •   Old Girdwood flooding at Gold Avenue and water quality concerns in drainage. – this is a DOT item related to
        culverts. Creek used to be dredged to improve drainage. Tuttle requests that an engineer look at the
       Girdwood Valley for recommendations on how to address the need for modernization of the drainage installed
       post-1964.

        9. PSAC Vacancy
Mike Opalka hasn’t formally resigned but has indicated that he is unable to continue serving on PSAC and plans to
move. Vacancy will be addressed at GBOS, which appoints PSAC members.

Reports/Ongoing items:
       10. Review recent/upcoming community events (see meeting packet)
            Forest Fair follow-up: Report received after this meeting and provided in the final meeting packet
           Coffee with cops/Kids and Cops: No planned events
       11. Other Community relations opportunities:
         PSAC member ride along with WPD
          Outreach via community resources: Newspaper; Newsletters; Clinic; Other
       12. Roundtable comments from the PSAC board
Amanda Tuttle has received reports from AWWU that indicate the utility has been out of compliance regarding
discharge in the mixing zone where treated sewage is discharged into Glacier Creek. She is reaching out to DEC and
EPA regarding a corrective action plan.

       13. Next meeting dates
           October 13 7PM
          Dec 15    7PM
         2027 dates TBA

Public Safety Reports:
WPD Update (WPD Chief Andre Achee) – review most recent stats: received and added to final meeting packet.
GFR Update (Chief Michelle Weston) – request written report
GBOS Public Safety Supervisor report

Public Comment: None

Adjourn: 9PM
